analyst_view.overall: Early view: Leganés are 17th with one point from their last seven league games, and Luis Carrión is still without a win since replacing Rubén Albés, the latest a 1-3 home defeat by Albacete in which Álvaro Morata missed an 86th-minute penalty. Burgos arrive third after Álex Forés's late winner against Celta Fortuna, but without Jon Karrikaburu (hamstring tear) and David González. Team news and the referee will be added the day before the Friday-night kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leganés have conceded seven in their last two league games (4-3 at Valladolid, 1-3 at home to Albacete) and have to chase this one at Butarque. Burgos have scored twice in three of their last four league games, even if Sergio Francisco says he does not want an end-to-end match.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean a little higher: Leganés had roughly two-thirds of the ball and 17 shots against Albacete, and Burgos used a back five against Castellón, a shape that invites crosses and blocked shots. Most of the extra should come at the Burgos end.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already a high figure, and I lean higher still. Leganés have just had Rubén Pulido and Yassine Kechta suspended at the same time, the site lists Francisco Montero as banned after a red card, and a side one point above the drop zone meets a Burgos team its coach calls the hardest-running in the league. No referee has been named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots. I lean lower: Sergio Francisco wants Burgos to have the ball and has ruled out an open game, so 12.5 away shots for them looks generous. Leganés should take most of the attempts, as they did with 17 against Albacete.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target and I see no strong reason to move it. Leganés create volume but finish poorly (no league win since 20 September, Morata's missed penalty last week), while Burgos are efficient rather than prolific, with Forés and Curro on four goals each.
